title: Four pillars, one problem
summary: Surgery, radiotherapy, systemic drugs and immunotherapy — the landmark results from aminopterin to sotorasib — and why tumours come back.

shots.title:
Four pillars,
one problem.
shots.subtitle: Surgery, radiation, drugs, immunity — and resistance.
shots.narration: Cancer treatment rests on four pillars. Each has computational problems inside it, and each fails in the same characteristic way: the tumour evolves.

shots.heading: The pillars
items: **Systemic drugs** — chemotherapy, targeted and hormonal therapy
**Immunotherapy** — release or engineer the immune response
shots.narration: Surgery removes the tumour. Radiotherapy damages tumour DNA with carefully planned beams. Systemic drugs reach the whole body. And immunotherapy releases or engineers the patient's own immune response.

shots.label: of new cancer patients should receive radiotherapy at least once
shots.narration: Radiotherapy is everywhere: an evidence-based model estimated that fifty-two percent of new cancer patients should receive it at least once. Planning each course is an optimisation problem.

events.label: CAR-T & tissue-agnostic
events.detail: engineered T cells; a biomarker-defined approval

shots.narration: Six landmarks: aminopterin in 1948; imatinib, designed against a single fusion kinase, approved in 2001; checkpoint immunotherapy proven in 2010; CAR-T and the first biomarker-defined approval in 2017; a Nobel in 2018; and KRAS drugged in 2021.

shots.text: Imatinib: find the **fusion kinase** that drives the leukaemia, design a drug against it — **53 of 54** patients responded.
shots.narration: Imatinib is the template for rational drug design. Chronic myeloid leukaemia is driven by the BCR-ABL fusion kinase. A drug designed to block it gave complete blood responses in fifty-three of fifty-four patients in its first trial.

shots.text: KRAS: picomolar affinity for GTP, no known pocket — **“undruggable”** until a new pocket was found in the G12C mutant (2013).
shots.narration: KRAS resisted for decades: it grips its GTP with picomolar affinity and offered no obvious pocket. In 2013 chemists found a new pocket in the G12C mutant, reachable through the mutant cysteine. Sotorasib followed, approved in 2021.

shots.label: hazard ratio for death with ipilimumab v. vaccine control
shots.context: metastatic melanoma, 676 patients · median survival 10.0 v. 6.4 months
shots.narration: Immunotherapy changed melanoma. In a six-hundred-and-seventy-six-patient trial, the checkpoint antibody ipilimumab raised median survival from six point four to ten months: a hazard ratio for death of zero point six eight.

shots.text: Checkpoint therapy releases the **brakes on T cells** — the 2018 Nobel Prize. CAR-T **engineers** them against a target.
shots.narration: Checkpoint drugs release brakes the tumour exploits to calm the immune system — the discovery recognised by the 2018 Nobel Prize. CAR-T goes further: the patient's own T cells are engineered to attack a target such as CD19.

shots.text: Why tumours come back: treatment **selects** the subline that already resisted it.
shots.narration: And why do tumours come back? Because treatment is a selection pressure. A variant subline that happens to resist the drug survives and regrows — exactly as Nowell predicted in 1976.

shots.text: Computation is inside every pillar: **beam planning**, **drug design**, **patient selection**, **combination scheduling**.
shots.narration: Computation sits inside every pillar: planning radiation beams, designing drugs, selecting patients by biomarker, and scheduling combinations. Those are the problems the rest of this course asks quantum methods to help with.

steps.title: Put the landmarks in order
steps.brief: Order these milestones in cancer treatment, earliest first.

items.label: Aminopterin gives temporary remissions in childhood leukaemia
Imatinib approved for chronic myeloid leukaemia
Ipilimumab extends survival in metastatic melanoma
A small-molecule pocket is found in KRAS G12C
First CAR-T therapy and first biomarker-defined, organ-agnostic approval
Sotorasib approved for KRAS G12C lung cancer

options: DNA replication in all dividing cells
questions.explain: BCR-ABL is the constitutively active kinase that drives chronic myeloid leukaemia.

questions.prompt: Why was KRAS long considered undruggable?
options: It is not mutated in cancer
It binds GTP/GDP with picomolar affinity and had no known allosteric pocket
questions.explain: Competing with GTP was hopeless; the G12C pocket offered another route.

questions.prompt: A hazard ratio for death of 0.68 means…
options: At any moment, the treated group died at about 68% of the control group's rate
questions.explain: A hazard ratio compares instantaneous event rates; it is not a cure rate or a change in median.

questions.prompt: What was new about the 2017 pembrolizumab approval for MSI-high tumours?
options: It was defined by a biomarker, not by the organ the cancer started in
questions.explain: Any unresectable or metastatic MSI-high or mismatch-repair-deficient solid tumour qualified.

steps.title: Homework 6 · A therapy, end to end
steps.brief: About 45 minutes. Pick one therapy and follow it from mechanism to failure.

fields.label: 1. Its mechanism, in your own words, at the level of molecules and cells.
2. One way tumours escape it, framed as clonal evolution. What would you measure to see it coming?
3. One computational problem inside this therapy (design, planning, selection, scheduling) and whether it has quantum-friendly structure.
